text:
If an SEO company promises you the #1 spot on Google, hang up.

Google's own guide says it plainly: no one can guarantee a #1 ranking.

The good ones talk about calls and enquiries, and can show you exactly what they did last month.

Picture an air con business in Joondalup.

Winter heater special in June. The special ended. The page stayed up.

Since October 12, Google Ads can pull offers off your website and show them in your ads.

Guess which deal customers are ringing up about.

Hiring someone to get you found on Google? Ask three things before you sign:

What exactly will you do each month?
Can I talk to a client you've helped?
Who owns my website and Business Profile if we part ways?

Vague answers are your answer.

Five minute Google Ads job:

Campaigns > Assets > three-dot menu > Account level automated assets > Advanced settings.

Switch off Automated promotions.

I'd rather you pick your own offers than let Google's AI dig through old pages on your site.

Old specials on your website are like a "Back in 5 minutes" sign from last Tuesday.

Nobody believes it, and now Google's ad system might read it out to your customers.

Take down every offer that's finished. Your ads and your SEO both get cleaner.

Asking ChatGPT for "a good physio in Subiaco" is the new word of mouth.

The answers still lean on the basics: your website, your Google Business Profile, your reviews.

I'd fix those before paying anyone for "AI SEO".
